title: A booked appointment never reaches the calendar — the create response is discarded and the refetch never fires
description:
Booking an appointment from the calendar's "New appointment" modal succeeds
server-side but never appears on the calendar. The clinician books, the dialog
closes, and the grid looks exactly as it did before — the appointment only
shows up after a manual page reload.

EVIDENCE — end-to-end run against a deployment, 2026-08-25, the booking spec:

* The Playwright network trace shows `POST /api/appointments` returning 201 and
  it is the LAST API call in the entire trace. There is no subsequent
  `GET /api/appointments?start=...&end=...`.
* The DOM captured at failure contains the patient booked by an EARLIER attempt
  (rendered because that page load fetched it) but not the patient booked
  moments before by this one.
* The 201 body is complete: it carries `patient_name` and `status: "confirmed"`,
  i.e. everything `EditorialCalendar` needs to render the event, including the
  field the calendar labels events from.

So this is not a server bug and not a rendering bug — the client simply never
learns that its own write happened.

The failure is intermittent in CI (three consecutive green runs, then red and
red again), which matches a race rather than a hard break. See the design field
for the suspected aggravator.

---

REOPENED 2026-08-26. pablo#742 merged and was closed as done; the bug is NOT
fixed. Verified against the deployment, not inferred.

Dev e2e run gh-32920420586 (2026-08-26 02:06), scheduling.spec.ts:85, still red
with the identical symptom. The fix IS deployed: build-frontend resolves the OSS
SHA from BASE_IMAGE.txt (deploy.yml "Resolve OSS SHA from BASE_IMAGE.txt") and
that was 6da9089b, which contains #742. So the cache write shipped and changed
nothing.

WHAT THE TRACE SHOWS

* POST /api/appointments -> 201, and it is STILL the last API call in the whole
  trace. No refetch, exactly as before the fix.
* The created row is well-formed: start_at 2026-08-26T01:59:00Z,
  status "confirmed", patient_name "E2E Patient-a26444d0" — everything the
  calendar needs to render it.
* It never reaches filteredAppointments. Proof independent of the DOM:
  dynamicDayWindow() expands the grid to contain ANY out-of-hours appointment,
  and the rendered grid still began at 08:00 while this appointment sits at
  01:59. Had it been in the list, the window would have opened to 1 AM.
* The booked patient appears in exactly 2 of 63 frame snapshots — the picker
  option and the modal's auto-title — and never on the grid.

WHAT THAT RULES OUT

Range containment (2026-08-23T00:00Z..2026-08-30T00:00Z contains 01:59Z), the
status filter (confirmed is on by default), a missing cache entry (the range GET
completed BEFORE the POST), and staleness (no refetch was even attempted).

WHERE TO LOOK NEXT — do NOT ship another blind fix

A cache write placed in the mutation's success path had no effect, which points
at the success path itself rather than at what it writes. Candidates, in order:

1. useAuthMutation's onSuccess never runs. In React Query v5 the options
   callbacks on useMutation are OBSERVER-level: if AppointmentModal unmounts
   before the mutation settles, they are skipped. handleSubmit passes
   `{ onSuccess: onClose }`, and onClose unmounts the modal — the dialog DOES
   close in the trace, which was the reason for assuming the chain ran, but
   that assumption has now been falsified by the fix not working.
2. useAuthQuery's `enabled: (options.enabled ?? true) && !loading` leaves the
   list query with no active observer during a Firebase token refresh, so a
   write notifies nothing and an invalidation refetches nothing. The trace
   shows THREE POST /api/login cycles in one run.

The way to settle it is a browser repro against dev with React Query devtools
open — book an appointment and watch whether onSuccess fires and whether the
cache entry changes. Minutes of observation beats hours of trace inference; two
rounds of the latter have now produced one ineffective fix.

Consider moving the write to the mutation CACHE level
(MutationCache.config.onSuccess), which survives observer unmount, if (1) is
confirmed.
design:
The write path already has the data it needs; it throws it away and asks the
cache to go find out again.

CURRENT SHAPE

`frontend/src/hooks/useAppointments.ts`:

    export function useCreateAppointment(token?: string) {
      return useAuthMutation({
        mutationFn: (data) => createAppointment(data, token),
        invalidateKeys: [queryKeys.appointments.all],   // <- shotgun, and a no-op here
      })
    }

`queryKeys.appointments.all` is `["appointments"]`, a prefix of every range list
AND every detail query, so one create invalidates the entire appointment cache.
That is wasteful even when it works — and in this flow it does not fire a
refetch at all.

THE FIX — adopt TanStack Query's "updates from mutation responses"

In `useCreateAppointment`'s success path, write the returned appointment into
the cached list(s) it belongs to instead of relying on a refetch:

1. Use the `optimistic` seam that `useAuthMutation` already exposes
   (`frontend/src/hooks/useAuthQuery.ts`), or an explicit `onSuccess`, to call
   `queryClient.setQueryData` for each cached
   `queryKeys.appointments.list({start, end})` entry whose range contains the
   created appointment's `start_at`. Append it to that entry's `data` array.
2. Iterate the existing cache rather than guessing the visible range: use
   `queryClient.getQueriesData({ queryKey: queryKeys.appointments.lists() })`
   so the currently-mounted week/month view is updated whatever it happens to
   be, and ranges that do not contain the appointment are left untouched.
3. Narrow the invalidation. Drop `queryKeys.appointments.all` in favour of
   `queryKeys.appointments.lists()` so unrelated detail queries survive.

A cache WRITE is the load-bearing part. It executes synchronously in the
mutation's success callback and does not depend on any query being active,
mounted, or enabled — which is what makes it immune to the race below.

SUSPECTED AGGRAVATOR — do not fix it here, but understand it

`useAuthQuery` merges `enabled: (options.enabled ?? true) && !loading`, where
`loading` comes from the auth context. While a token refresh is in flight the
calendar's list query is DISABLED. `invalidateQueries` defaults to
`refetchType: "active"`, and a disabled query has no active observer to refetch
— so an invalidation landing inside that window is silently dropped. The trace
for the failing run shows three `POST /api/login` cycles, which is consistent
with the intermittency.

This is a plausible mechanism, NOT a proven one; it has not been reproduced
locally. It is written down so the next person does not re-derive it. Fixing
the `enabled` gating is a much wider change (it touches every query in the app)
and belongs in its own bead — do not take it on here.

RECURRING CREATES

`useCreateRecurringAppointment` creates a series, so a single-record splice does
not apply. Narrowing its `invalidateKeys` to `queryKeys.appointments.lists()`
is sufficient and is all that is asked for. Do not attempt to synthesise
occurrences client-side.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate

* The cache write is the fix. Do not "invalidate harder"
  (`refetchType: "all"`, `refetchInterval`, forced remounts) as the primary
  remedy — that leaves the create path dependent on timing.
* Do NOT modify `frontend/src/hooks/useAuthQuery.ts`. Its `enabled` gating is a
  separate concern with app-wide blast radius.
* Do NOT touch `frontend/src/components/sessions/UploadTranscriptDialog.tsx` or
  anything in the error-interceptor path — PABLO-5r5 owns that file.
* Do NOT change the end-to-end spec's assertions. The spec asserts the booked
  patient's name becomes visible without a reload; that assertion is correct and
  the product is what is wrong.
* Server-initiated appointment changes (an appointment created by something
  other than this client) are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE. That needs a
  server-to-client channel and is its own bead.

FILES EXPECTED

* frontend/src/hooks/useAppointments.ts  (the change)
* frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/useAppointments.test.ts or a sibling test file
  (new coverage)

=== SECOND-OPINION REVIEW, 2026-08-26 03:00. READ BEFORE TOUCHING THIS. ===

RULED OUT — do not spend time re-deriving these:

* "The fix was never deployed." FALSE, checked by timestamp. Deploy Frontend to
  Dev completed 2026-08-26T01:32:21Z; the failing e2e started 01:49:39Z and
  created its appointment at 01:59:00Z. The trace exercised the FIXED bundle.
* "The modal unmounts, so onSuccess is skipped." Irrelevant either way.
  AppointmentForm (which owns the hooks, AppointmentModal.tsx:316) DOES unmount
  with Radix's DialogPrimitive.Root — but in react-query v5 only MUTATE-level
  callbacks are gated on hasListeners(). Hook-level onSuccess runs from the
  cache-owned Mutation.execute regardless. The cache write survives unmount.
* "A Firebase token refresh disables the list query mid-session." FALSE.
  useFirebaseAuthState (frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/client.ts:211-233) sets
  loading=true once and clears it in a finally on the FIRST onIdTokenChanged
  tick; it never flips back. The three POST /api/login in the trace are
  syncAuthTick cookie syncs and do not touch `loading`. Also note a disabled
  query still receives setQueryData and re-renders — `enabled` gates FETCHING
  only, so this could never have explained the write not showing.
* Key identity. The onSuccess writes to keys it read back out of the cache via
  getQueriesData prefix-matched on ["appointments","list"], so it cannot miss by
  construction. One QueryClient (root providers.tsx), one react-query copy, and
  the SaaS queryKeys.extensions.ts does not touch `appointments`.

THE STRONGEST REMAINING LEAD

getAuthHeader (frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts:249-262) awaits
getClientAuthProvider().getIdToken() with NO timeout — unlike syncAuthTick,
which wraps its token calls in withTimeout. A wedged token refresh leaves the
refetch parked in fetchStatus "fetching" having never opened a socket. That
matches the trace exactly: no GET at all, and a reload fixes it. Unproven —
verify before building on it.

DO THIS

1. Reproduce in a browser against dev with React Query devtools open. Book an
   appointment and watch (a) whether onSuccess fires, (b) whether the list
   cache entry gains the row, (c) whether a refetch is dispatched and what its
   fetchStatus is. Minutes of observation beats hours of trace inference; two
   rounds of the latter produced one ineffective fix.
2. Whatever the cause, restore the invalidation #742 removed. The correct
   pattern is setQueryData for instant UX PLUS
   invalidateQueries({queryKey: queryKeys.appointments.lists()}) for truth —
   server-computed fields, ordering, `total`, and ranges the walk missed. A
   manual append is an optimization, never the sole consistency mechanism.
3. If the lead above is confirmed, wrap getIdToken() in getAuthHeader with the
   same withTimeout used by syncAuthTick. An unbounded token await silently
   starves every refetch queued behind it, app-wide.

=== REPRODUCED LOCALLY 2026-08-26 03:45. Deterministic. ===

Run against dev with the pinned user, TZ=UTC, book from the calendar UI:

  FRESH patient (created via scenarios.givePatient, selected by TYPING to
  search):  appointment does NOT appear on the grid. exact=0, loose=0.
  EXISTING patient (picked by clicking the first option, no typing):
  appointment appears INSTANTLY. exact=1.

Same page, same session, same week, minutes apart. That is the discriminator,
and it is why this looked unreproducible: booking "just works" if you pick a
patient that was already in the picker.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG (measured, not assumed)

* The server persists it. The post-reload GET returns the row every time
  (contains created id = true).
* The list carries the label. rows carrying patient_name: 32/32, and the row
  for the created appointment has patient_name AND title populated.
* It renders after a reload. exact patient_name = 1.
* The POST response is well formed: patient_name set, status "confirmed",
  start_at inside the cached range (created 03:40Z, cached range
  2026-08-23T00:00Z..2026-08-30T00:00Z).
* dynamicDayWindow expands correctly for out-of-hours times — under TZ=UTC the
  grid rendered from 2 AM. The earlier "grid still starts at 8 AM, therefore it
  is not in the list" inference was WRONG; that grid was simply scrolled.

WHAT IS WRONG

Network trace of the failing case, in order:

  03:38:36  GET  /api/appointments?start=2026-08-23...&end=2026-08-30...
  03:38:38  POST /api/appointments
  (nothing further)

No GET after the POST — the invalidation #742 removed is genuinely absent — AND
the cache append does not land in this path either. Both mechanisms miss, which
is why the grid stays empty until a reload.

STILL UNKNOWN — the one experiment left

Whether the discriminator is "the patient is newly created" or "the picker was
TYPED into to search" (the fresh-patient path does both). The isolating run —
existing patient, selected BY TYPING — was killed by a transient Firebase MFA
400 from repeated sign-ins, not by the bug. Re-run that one first; it is two
minutes and it splits the remaining space in half.

BEARING ON pablo#747

#747 restores invalidateQueries(lists()) alongside the append. The trace above
shows the missing refetch is exactly what is absent in the failing path, so
#747 is now a plausible FIX rather than only a robustness improvement — but it
has not been verified against this reproduction. Verify before closing.

HOW TO REPRODUCE

Scratch spec (not committed): book from /dashboard/calendar after
scenarios.givePatient, type the last name into the Patient combobox, pick the
option, Schedule, then count getByText(patient_name, {exact:true}) BEFORE any
reload. Run with:
  TZ=UTC E2E_USE_PINNED=1 bash e2e/scripts/run-local.sh specs/<spec>.ts

=== ISOLATED 2026-08-26 04:00 — it is the NEW PATIENT, not the typing ===

Two bookings, same run, same page, same week, both selected BY TYPING into the
picker:

  EXISTING patient  -> name-matches = 8   (renders instantly)
  FRESH patient     -> name-matches = 0   (renders only after reload)

So typing/search is NOT the trigger. A patient created moments earlier is.

The card is not merely unlabelled — it is absent. EditorialEventCard renders
`patientName ?? appointment.title`, so an unlabelled card would still print
"<name> — Individual", and a SUBSTRING match on the patient name would find it.
The substring count was 0, so no card exists: the appointment never reaches
filteredAppointments, i.e. the cache append does not land in this path.

WHY THIS MAKES pablo#747 THE LIKELY FIX

The failing path has NO refetch (POST is the last call) and NO working append.
Both mechanisms are missing at once, which is exactly the hole #742 opened when
it replaced invalidation with an append instead of adding one. #747 restores
invalidateQueries(lists()) alongside the append, and the server demonstrably
HAS the row (the post-reload GET returns it, with patient_name, every time) —
so a refetch would render it.

VERIFY THIS WAY — do not close on reasoning alone

Re-run the two-case isolation above against a deployment carrying #747. FRESH
must reach a non-zero name-match count BEFORE any reload. If it still reads 0,
#747 is not the fix and the append failure is a separate defect worth its own
investigation — in that case instrument useCreateAppointment's onSuccess
directly (log the getQueriesData key list and the chosen ranges) rather than
inferring from the DOM again.

OPEN QUESTION WORTH A LOOK EITHER WAY

usePatientList() in EditorialCalendar holds ONE page of the roster, and a
just-created patient is not in it. patient_name on the appointment normally
makes patientMap irrelevant, so this should not matter — but "the fresh patient
is the discriminator" and "the roster cache is stale for exactly that patient"
are suspicious neighbours. If #747 does not fix it, look here next.

=== VERIFIED AGAINST #747 (dev, base bc04f4c, 2026-08-26 04:40) — NOT FIXED ===

Two bookings, same run, same page, both selected BY TYPING. Network calls to
/api/appointments, in order:

  FRESH patient     GET | POST                 -> 0 on grid   STILL BROKEN
  EXISTING patient  GET | POST | GET           -> 9 on grid   works

#747's invalidation DOES fire — but only for an existing patient. For a fresh
one there is no refetch at all. Same hook, same callback, same code path.

WHY THAT IS THE SHARPEST CLUE YET

useAuthMutation runs the two steps sequentially and unguarded:

    onSuccess: (data, variables) => {
      options.onSuccess?.(data, variables, queryClient)     // #742's cache walk
      if (!options.optimistic) invalidate(variables, data)  // #747's refetch
    }

The refetch is the NEXT STATEMENT after the walk. Observing the refetch fire in
one case and not the other means execution is leaving that callback early in
the fresh case — the walk aborts, and takes the invalidation with it.

NOT YET EXPLAINED — read before assuming it throws

If options.onSuccess threw, react-query v5's Mutation.execute would take the
error path, the mutation would settle as an error, and the MUTATE-level
onSuccess (onClose) would never run — so the dialog would stay open. The dialog
DOES close. Those two facts are in tension and one of them must be wrong.
Resolve that before writing a fix.

Also observed in the fresh flow and NOT yet attributed: a 403 response. The URL
was not captured — the run that would have logged it was killed by Firebase MFA
throttling (repeated sign-ins). Capturing that URL is the single cheapest next
datum.

NEXT STEPS, CHEAPEST FIRST

1. Re-run the two-case isolation logging every response >= 400 with its URL.
   Wait out the MFA throttle first, or reuse one signed-in session for both
   cases instead of signing in twice.
2. Add temporary logging inside useCreateAppointment's onSuccess (entry, the
   getQueriesData key list, each range decision, exit) and read it off the
   browser console. Stop inferring the callback's behaviour from the network.
3. Only then decide the fix. A try/finally around options.onSuccess in
   useAuthMutation — so a caller's callback can never silently disable cache
   invalidation — is defensible on its own merits REGARDLESS of this bug, but
   do not ship it as "the fix" until the tension above is resolved.

WHAT #747 DID ACHIEVE

The invalidation is real and works wherever the callback completes. It is a
genuine robustness improvement and should stay. It is simply not sufficient,
because in the failing path the callback does not reach it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Creating an appointment from the calendar's "New appointment" modal makes it
   appear on the grid with no page reload and no second `GET /api/appointments`
   round-trip. Verifiable in a browser and in the network panel: the only
   appointment-related request is the `POST`.
2. Unit test: with a cached list entry for a range that CONTAINS the created
   appointment's `start_at`, the create mutation's success path leaves that
   entry containing the new appointment, sourced from the mutation response
   (assert on `patient_name`, proving the response body was used rather than a
   refetch).
3. Unit test: a cached list entry for a range that does NOT contain the created
   appointment's `start_at` is left byte-for-byte unchanged.
4. `useCreateAppointment` no longer invalidates `queryKeys.appointments.all`. A
   cached `queryKeys.appointments.detail(<unrelated id>)` entry is still present
   and not marked invalid after a create.
5. `useCreateRecurringAppointment` invalidates `queryKeys.appointments.lists()`
   and not `queryKeys.appointments.all`; creating a weekly series still results
   in its occurrences rendering on the calendar.
6. `frontend/src/hooks/useAuthQuery.ts` is unmodified by this change.
7. `make check` passes in this repo (lint incl. mypy, plus tests). Frontend unit
   tests pass.

title: Appointment modal patient picker: say when the roster is truncated
description:
AppointmentModal's patient picker requests the roster at the list endpoint's cap
(`usePatientList({ page_size: 100, search })`) and renders whatever comes back.
When a practice has more patients than that cap, the listbox silently shows the
alphabetical first 100 with nothing telling the user either that (a) the list is
truncated, or (b) typing searches the full roster server-side.

Booking the overflow patient still WORKS — you just have to know to type. A
clinician who opens the picker, scrolls to the bottom, and does not find their
patient has no reason to believe typing would help. That is the whole defect:
a missing affordance, not a missing capability.

Concretely, from the pinned E2E tenant on the 2026-08-21 dev run:
  GET /api/patients?page_size=100  ->  { total: 163, page_size: 100, data: [100] }
  the window ends at "Patient-5b654369"; "Patient-5ce55021" is simply absent.

This is the affordance gap sitting behind pablo-saas THERAPY-ec9za. The
FUNCTIONAL fix — server-side search — already shipped in pablo#704; this bead is
only about telling the user the list is partial.
design:
frontend/src/components/calendar/AppointmentModal.tsx

The list endpoint already returns the numbers needed: the response shape is
`{ data, total, page, page_size }`, and the modal currently keeps only
`patientData?.data`. Thread `total` through as well.

`PatientCombobox` today takes { patients, patientId, fallbackLabel, onSelect,
query, onQueryChange }. Add `total` (number) to that prop list.

When `total > patients.length` AND there is no active query, render a
non-interactive footer <li> as the last child of the existing role="listbox"
<ul>, reading e.g. "Showing first 100 of 163 — type to search".

Two constraints that matter:
  * The footer MUST NOT carry role="option". It is not selectable, and an
    extra option would pollute option-based test locators (scheduling.spec.ts
    picks by getByRole("option", ...)) and break keyboard navigation.
  * Render it ONLY when the query is empty. Once the user is searching, the
    returned rows are a filtered result and "showing first 100 of 163" would be
    actively misleading.

Style it like the existing empty-state row ("No patients found"), which already
uses `px-3 py-2 text-[13px]` with `color: var(--ed-ink-soft)`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Roster larger than the cap, empty query: the listbox shows a truncation hint
   naming the loaded count and the true total, and inviting search.
2. The hint is not role="option", is not selectable by click or keyboard, and
   does not change the number of options the picker exposes.
3. Roster at or under the cap: no hint renders.
4. Active search query: no hint renders, regardless of counts.
5. Existing AppointmentModal unit tests and pablo-saas scheduling e2e are
   unaffected; `make check` passes.
notes:
Split out of the THERAPY-ec9za investigation (2026-08-21) at Kurt's request. Purely an affordance fix — do not change the 100 cap or re-plumb search; both are already correct.
P0 per Kurt 2026-08-21 (the affordance gap sits behind a red scheduling e2e). PROMOTED llama-ok (promotion pass 2026-08-21): trigger walk — frontend-only affordance in AppointmentModal/PatientCombobox; no patient data handling changes, no money, no infra, no auth, no vendor, no claim-adjacent constructs, nothing outbound. Design + acceptance already complete; footer must not carry role=option (pinned by acceptance #2).

title: [SaaS-facing] Trial-limit wall is occluded by the transcript-upload dialog — write dialogs must stand down when an interceptor already explained the error
description:
Hitting the free-trial session cap from the transcript-upload flow shows the
user a raw "API request failed with status 402" inside the still-open "Upload
Session Transcript" dialog. The SaaS overlay's upgrade wall (UpgradePromptDialog,
opened by TrialLimitDialogHost) DOES render — but it renders underneath that
dialog and is completely occluded, so the explanation the wall exists to give
never reaches the user.

This is the exact failure mode pablo-saas#2249 ("a wall that explains itself")
was written to eliminate, reintroduced by dialog stacking rather than by the
wall being missing.

EVIDENCE — dev e2e run 2026-08-21, trial-lifecycle.spec.ts:207:
  * Screenshot: only the upload dialog is visible, carrying the literal text
    "API request failed with status 402". The wall is nowhere on screen.
  * Page snapshot: `- button: Request a 4-day extension` IS present in the DOM,
    but only the upload dialog's nodes carry Playwright refs — the wall sits
    outside the top-most modal and is therefore out of the accessibility tree.
    That is why the spec's getByText assertions (title, "15 of 15 trial
    sessions") PASS while the getByRole button assertion reports
    "element(s) not found".
  * Artifacts: gs://pablohealth-dev-e2e-artifacts/manual-verify-timeout-1200/
    test-results/trial-lifecycle--trial-lif-9e260-e-read-only-with-trial-copy-chromium/

NOT a copy drift: GRACE_EXTENSION_HOURS = 96 and the button already reads
"Request a 4-day extension" on main. The copy and the wall are both correct;
only the stacking is wrong.
design:
The seam already exists and is unused.

frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts runs `apiErrorInterceptors` and merges whatever
they return onto the thrown ApiError (`Object.assign(apiError, interceptorData)`,
~line 324). The SaaS overlay's `trialLimitInterceptor` already returns
`{ trialLimitReached: true }` with the stated intent "so the failed caller can
mute its own generic error copy" — but nothing in OSS ever reads it.

Add a GENERIC, provider-agnostic contract rather than teaching OSS about billing:

1. frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts — declare an optional `handledExternally?:
   boolean` field on the `ApiError` class, documented as: "a registered error
   interceptor has already surfaced an explanation to the user (a dialog, a
   flash). Callers must not render their own generic error copy, and a caller
   that is itself a modal must close so that explanation is not occluded."
   OSS stays ignorant of WHY it was handled — only THAT it was.

2. frontend/src/components/sessions/UploadTranscriptDialog.tsx — both error
   paths set `setUploadError(message)` today: the `onError` callback (~line 241)
   and the `catch` in the async submit path (~line 215). In each, when
   `error instanceof ApiError && error.handledExternally`, skip
   `setUploadError(...)` and call `onClose()` instead of leaving the dialog open.

SCOPE: UploadTranscriptDialog is the ONLY OSS component that creates sessions
(the write that `_gate_trial_session` gates), so it is the only required call
site. These other components also render inline API error copy and may adopt
the same rule later — explicitly OUT of scope here: DiagnosesTab,
MedicationsTab, OutcomeMeasuresTab, PatientChartTabs, PatientDocuments,
SessionsTable.

PAIRED SaaS CHANGE (separate bead, pablo-saas THERAPY-1431q):
`trialLimitInterceptor` in frontend/overlay/src/lib/api/client.extensions.ts
returns `handledExternally: true` alongside `trialLimitReached: true`. Until
that lands, this OSS change is INERT — which is the safe landing order: OSS
first, then the overlay, then a dev deploy.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With a trial at its session cap, submitting the transcript-upload dialog
   closes that dialog and leaves UpgradePromptDialog visible AND interactive

title: Rate limiters sharing a Redis key silently share one window
description:
Found while splitting the public-booking rate limit on 2026-08-20. NOT specific to booking links — pre-existing, and it disables limits that look enforced.

RedisSlidingWindow builds its key as f'{KEY_PREFIX}{key}' — purely the string it is handed. Separation between limiters therefore has to live in the KEY, not in holding distinct limiter objects. Two problems follow:

1. Cross-endpoint collision. routes/chat.py:572, routes/sessions.py:1181 and routes/ehr_routes.py:158 all call .check(user.id) with a bare user id. On the Redis path (multi-instance Cloud Run) chat send, audio upload and EHR navigate share ONE sorted set at ratelimit:{user_id}, so each endpoint consumes the others' budget.

2. CompositeLimiter's windows fight each other. get_chat_send_limiter and get_audio_upload_limiter each build a CompositeLimiter of a 60s and a 3600s window, both handed the same key. The per-minute limiter's zremrangebyscore deletes everything older than 60s from the shared set, so the per-hour window can never accumulate past a minute's worth — the per-hour limits (chat_rate_per_hour, upload_rate_per_hour) are effectively DEAD on the Redis path.

The in-memory limiter has the same shape (dict keyed on the raw string), so single-instance self-hosts are affected too.

Fix: namespace every limiter's key, and give CompositeLimiter's sub-windows distinct suffixes. The new public-booking limiters already prefix theirs (public-booking: / public-booking-write:) and test_rate_limit.py pins the independence — use that as the pattern.
design:
VERIFIED SURFACES (2026-08-20 investigation that filed this bead; re-verify line numbers at build time): RedisSlidingWindow builds its key as f'{KEY_PREFIX}{key}' — separation between limiters lives entirely in the key string. Call sites passing a bare user id: routes/chat.py:572, routes/sessions.py:1181, routes/ehr_routes.py:158 — on the Redis path (multi-instance deployments) chat send, audio upload and EHR navigate share ONE sorted set at ratelimit:{user_id}, so each endpoint consumes the others' budget. CompositeLimiter: get_chat_send_limiter and get_audio_upload_limiter each stack a 60s and a 3600s window on the SAME key, so the per-minute window's zremrangebyscore prunes everything older than 60s and the per-hour limits (chat_rate_per_hour, upload_rate_per_hour) can never trip — dead on the Redis path. The in-memory limiter has the same shape (dict keyed on the raw string), so single-instance deployments are affected too.

PLAN:
(1) Namespace every limiter's key at limiter construction — a per-endpoint prefix (e.g. chat-send: / audio-upload: / ehr-nav:), following the pattern the public-booking limiters already use (public-booking: / public-booking-write:) and that test_rate_limit.py pins for independence.
(2) CompositeLimiter hands each sub-window a distinct key suffix (e.g. :60s / :3600s) so no two windows ever share a sorted set.
(3) Apply the same keying to the in-memory limiter path.

PRE-ANSWERED: key shapes change; stale un-namespaced Redis windows simply age out — no migration, no flag. Limit VALUES are untouched; this bead is key isolation only. Prefer fixing the key inside the limiter factories over editing every route call site, so future limiters cannot recreate the bug.

FILES: the rate-limit module defining RedisSlidingWindow / CompositeLimiter / the get_*_limiter factories; route call sites only if keys are built there; test_rate_limit.py.

DONE SIGNAL: red-then-green — a test proving the per-hour window survives per-minute pruning on the Redis path fails on current main and passes with the change; plus a test that chat/audio/EHR budgets are independent. make check green.
acceptance_criteria: Each limiter keys into its own namespace; CompositeLimiter sub-windows do not share a key; a test proves the per-hour window survives per-minute pruning on the Redis path; chat/audio/EHR budgets are independent.

Backend-only, red-then-green test defined.

title: Email seam: EmailSender protocol + EMAIL_BACKEND contract
description:
Everything in phase 2 that establishes identity needs outbound email, and the engine has none (reminders log today). Specify and build the seam before the things that hang off it.

Per docs/design/public-booking.md 'The email seam': an EmailSender protocol, an EMAIL_BACKEND setting selecting the adapter, and failure/privacy semantics. The 'none' backend must REFUSE to arm confirmation-dependent paths rather than pretend to send — a silent no-op here means bookings that never confirm.

Blocks the confirmation work.
design:
The contract is already written. docs/design/public-booking.md "The email seam"
(§ Protocol, § Backend selection, § Failure and privacy semantics) specifies
this in full. Build that, do not redesign it. What follows is where it goes in
this tree and which decisions are already closed.

WHAT SHIPS

One new module, backend/app/services/email_sender.py:

* `OutboundEmail` dataclass — `to`, `subject`, `text`, `kind`.
* `EmailSender` Protocol — a single `send(message: OutboundEmail) -> None`.
* `NoneEmailSender` — logs the `kind` and succeeds. This is the default, so a
  bare deployment behaves exactly as it does today.
* `SmtpEmailSender` — `smtplib` with STARTTLS.
* `InMemoryEmailSender` — captures messages for tests, mirroring the in-memory
  repositories.
* `email_sender_from_settings(settings) -> EmailSender` — mirror
  `file_storage_from_settings` at the bottom of
  backend/app/services/file_storage.py (~line 549): same shape, same position
  in the file, same docstring register.

Settings (backend/app/settings.py): `email_backend: Literal["none", "smtp"]`
defaulting to `"none"`, declared the way `file_storage_provider` (~line 697)
and `transcription_provider` (~line 661) already are. Plus `smtp_host`,
`smtp_port`, `smtp_username`, `smtp_password` (SecretStr), `smtp_from`.

THE REFUSAL SIGNAL — the point of the bead

A `none` backend that silently succeeds is the whole hazard: a booking that
depends on a confirmation email would be accepted and then never confirm, with
nothing anywhere saying why. So the seam must let a delivery-dependent caller
TELL, and refuse to arm.

Closed: a `can_deliver: bool` on the protocol — False on `NoneEmailSender`,
True on `SmtpEmailSender` and `InMemoryEmailSender`. A caller that requires
delivery checks it and refuses. Chosen over re-reading settings at each call
site: one place to be wrong, and trivially fakeable in a test.

PRIVACY — load-bearing, will be checked

A recipient address on an appointment implies a care relationship, so it is
PHI-adjacent and guardrail #5 applies. NO backend may log the address, the
subject, or the body. `NoneEmailSender` logs `kind` alone; `SmtpEmailSender`
logs success or failure with no addressee. Bodies stay minimal by contract —
time, duration, host name, a manage link, nothing clinical, whatever agreements
a deployment's provider has signed.

FAILURE SEMANTICS

`send()` RAISES on failure. It does not swallow. The doc's "best-effort side
effect" posture (a failed confirmation must never fail the booking) is then the
caller's to implement by catching and logging — which is also why verification
sends, whose failure must surface, need no special case here. Encode the rule
in the docstring. No retry, no queue, no backoff in this bead.

SCOPE — this bead ships the SEAM ONLY, with no consumer wired

Do NOT touch, in this bead:

* backend/app/services/reminder_service.py — leave its `_send_24h_reminder` /
  `_send_1h_reminder` logging exactly as it is.
* Any route, and anything under backend/app/scheduling_engine/.
* Verification tokens, confirmation flows, booking links — PABLO-e3a.2 and its
  siblings own those and are blocked on this.

A note for whoever wires reminders later, NOT this bead's job: today
reminder_service.py flips `reminder_24h_sent = True` whether or not anything
was sent. The design doc requires those flags to flip only on success, so that
line has to change when a real sender is attached. Filed here so it is not
rediscovered.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate

* SMTP first, no vendor SDK. Every provider speaks it, and the mail
  relationship — including any compliance agreement it needs — stays the
  deployment's own. Further adapters go behind the same protocol later; the
  engine never hard-codes a vendor.
* `kind` is for logging and tests. It is NEVER used to route to a provider.
* `none` is the default. Do not make `smtp` the default "because it is more
  useful".
* Plain text only. The HTML field is explicitly deferred by the design doc.
* `can_deliver` is the refusal mechanism, per above.

FILES EXPECTED

* backend/app/services/email_sender.py (new)
* backend/app/settings.py (new settings only)
* a new test module under backend/tests/
acceptance_criteria:
1. backend/app/services/email_sender.py defines `OutboundEmail` with fields
   `to`, `subject`, `text`, `kind`, and an `EmailSender` Protocol whose only
   method is `send(message: OutboundEmail) -> None` — matching the signatures
   in docs/design/public-booking.md "Protocol".
2. `email_backend` exists in Settings as `Literal["none", "smtp"]` defaulting to
   `"none"`. `email_sender_from_settings()` returns `NoneEmailSender` on a
   default Settings and `SmtpEmailSender` when `email_backend="smtp"`.
3. `NoneEmailSender.send()` returns normally, and a test using caplog asserts
   that across ALL emitted records the recipient address, the subject, and the
   body text each appear zero times.
4. `SmtpEmailSender` calls STARTTLS before login (assert ordering against a
   fake smtplib), reads host/port/username/password/from from Settings, and
   types the password as `SecretStr`. A caplog assertion proves no record
   contains the recipient address.
5. `can_deliver` is False on `NoneEmailSender` and True on both
   `SmtpEmailSender` and `InMemoryEmailSender`, asserted directly.
6. `InMemoryEmailSender` records every sent `OutboundEmail` in send order and is
   importable from the same module for use as a test double.
7. A delivery failure propagates: with a fake smtplib raising, `send()` raises
   rather than returning — asserted with pytest.raises. The docstring states
   that best-effort swallowing is the caller's responsibility.
8. No consumer is wired. The diff touches no file under backend/app/routes/ or
   backend/app/scheduling_engine/, and backend/app/services/reminder_service.py
   is byte-for-byte unchanged.
9. `make check` passes — lint including mypy, plus the test suite.

title: Natural-language availability rule entry
description: Availability rules are entered through a structured form only: pick a rule type from a dropdown, fill typed params. "No appointments on Fridays" requires knowing that means "Block day of week → Friday". A free-text entry point — type the rule as a sentence, see the structured rule it parses to, confirm to create — makes the availability system usable the way people actually think about their schedule, and belongs on the same surface as the structured editor it feeds.
design:
SPEC (spec pass 2026-08-18, drafting agent; verified against main at 771dd2b4). Two-stage propose-then-confirm natural-language entry for availability rules — the model NEVER writes a rule directly.

CLOSED DECISIONS carried forward — do not re-litigate: propose-then-confirm, never silent creation; parse output constrained to the existing rule_type/params schemas (no new rule types introduced by this bead); the structured form remains the primary editor and is not redesigned; deterministic date/day arithmetic stays in existing code paths — the LLM maps words to rule parameters, it does not compute dates; do not touch the engine's slot computation or conflict checking.

MECHANISM, verified pointers:

1. PARSE ENDPOINT — POST /api/availability/rules/parse, a sync route appended to the availability section of backend/app/routes/scheduling.py (beside create_availability_rule :754-786). Auth is the identical dependency every sibling rule route uses — ctx: TenantContext = Depends(get_tenant_context) (:743, :761; resolver backend/app/auth/service.py:406-431) — no new auth surface, and the route is read-only: it never touches the rule repository. Request/response Pydantic models live with the other scheduling models in backend/app/models/scheduling.py (availability block :128-160):
   - ParseAvailabilityRulesRequest { text: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=1000) }
   - ProposedAvailabilityRule { rule_type: str, enforcement: str, params: dict[str, Any], human_summary: str }
   - ParseAvailabilityRulesResponse { proposals: list[ProposedAvailabilityRule], could_not_parse: str | None = None }
   Decided: semantic outcomes are HTTP 200 (proposals, or proposals=[] plus a could_not_parse reason — "could not parse" is a product outcome, not a transport error); malformed requests are Pydantic 422; gateway/transport failure surfaces as the standard 500-class ServerError. Rate limiting: new get_availability_parse_limiter in backend/app/rate_limit.py mirroring get_ehr_navigate_limiter (:187-202), backed by a new settings field availability_parse_daily_limit (int, default 100, ge=1) beside ehr_navigate_daily_limit (backend/app/settings.py:869-873); checked at the top of the route with .check(ctx.user_id) exactly as backend/app/routes/ehr_routes.py:158 does.

2. PARSE SERVICE — new backend/app/services/availability_parse_service.py mirroring NoteImportService (backend/app/services/note_import_service.py:422-486): class AvailabilityRuleParseService(llm_gateway: StructuredLLMGateway | None = None, model: str | None = None), gateway defaulting via get_default_structured_llm_gateway (structured_llm_gateway.py:618-629). Model resolution mirrors note-import's mechanical-extraction choice (:435-441): settings.ai_model_flash falling back to settings.ai_model (backend/app/settings.py:954, :945) — mapping a sentence onto a fixed schema is mechanical, not generative. Call shape: complete_structured (abstract signature backend/app/services/structured_llm_gateway.py:97-107) with temperature=0.0, thinking_budget=0 (same rationale as note_import_service.py:463-471) and a fixed max_output_tokens=2048. Schema enforcement is the gateway's own response_mime_type="application/json" + response_schema mechanism (:171-174); all gateway implementations share the abstract signature, so provider stays a config concern.
   DB seam: the route calls release_db_connection() (backend/app/db/__init__.py:262) before invoking the service — the same seam as the note-import route (backend/app/routes/sessions.py:463-472) — and the gateway hard-enforces it via assert_no_held_db_connection (structured_llm_gateway.py:158-160; guard defined at backend/app/db/__init__.py:316).

3. RULE-TYPE SOURCE OF TRUTH, decided: the backend RuleType enum (backend/app/scheduling_engine/models/availability.py:13-21). The prompt's type list, the response_schema, and the post-hoc validator are all built in the service from a spec keyed by RuleType members. Why backend, not the frontend list: frontend/src/types/availability.ts:12-23 documents itself as a mirror of the backend enum; the create route validates rule_type with RuleType() (scheduling.py:766); and the engine reads the params keys directly (services/availability.py:171-176 etc.). A unit test pins the covered set so enum growth fails loudly and coverage widens deliberately, never implicitly.
   Day convention: day_of_week is 0=Monday — the engine compares proposed_start.weekday() (services/availability.py:171-172, :192, :329-334) and the frontend DAY_OPTIONS agree (AvailabilitySettings.tsx:31-39). The prompt states this explicitly; "Fridays" maps to 4.

4. VALIDATION IS THE SERVICE'S JOB — verified gap: the create API does not validate params at all (CreateAvailabilityRuleRequest.params is a bare dict[str, Any], models/scheduling.py:133) and the engine indexes params keys directly, so the parse service validates every proposal itself with pure per-type functions (working_hours: day_of_week 0-6, HH:MM, start<end; block_day_of_week: day_of_week 0-6; block_time_range: HH:MM, start<end; max_per_day: max>=1; buffer_before/after: minutes>=0) — mirroring the frontend validate() (AvailabilitySettings.tsx:163-191). A gateway response whose rule_type is outside the covered set or whose params fail validation is REJECTED into could_not_parse — never passed through as a proposal.

5. RULE COVERAGE, decided at spec time: v1 parses the six date-free types — working_hours, block_day_of_week, block_time_range, max_per_day, buffer_before, buffer_after. block_date_range and block_specific_dates are OUT of v1: date-bearing sentences are dominantly relative ("block next Friday", "the week of Thanksgiving") or year-ambiguous ("Dec 24"), and mapping them correctly requires calendar arithmetic against today's date — exactly what the closed no-date-math decision forbids the model to do; an "absolute fully-qualified dates only" carve-out is a guess factory with no clean boundary. Consequence, also decided: the prompt receives NO today's-date or timezone context at all — the parse is time-invariant and its tests are clock-free. Date-ish input returns could_not_parse with a reason pointing the user at the date pickers in the structured form. Any settings-owned rule type that lands in the enum later stays excluded automatically: the covered set is an explicit frozenset, not "all RuleType members".

6. MULTIPLE PROPOSALS — compound sentences return a list; each proposal is individually confirmable. "9 to 5 on weekdays" yields five working_hours proposals (day_of_week 0..4, start "09:00", end "17:00"). Decided: enforcement defaults to "hard" (the form default, models/scheduling.py:132); the prompt may propose "soft" only for explicit preference language ("I'd prefer not to…"), and the user can flip it in the edit step regardless.

7. CONFIRM (frontend) — new component file frontend/src/components/settings/NaturalLanguageRuleEntry.tsx, mounted in AvailabilitySettings with a single import + single JSX insertion between the list-error block and the RuleForm/Add-rule block (AvailabilitySettings.tsx:710-716 today). Plumbing mirrors the existing generic CRUD: a parseAvailabilityRules() POST wrapper in frontend/src/lib/api/availability.ts (beside createAvailabilityRule :23-28) and a useParseAvailabilityRules mutation in frontend/src/hooks/useAvailability.ts (useAuthMutation, no invalidateKeys — read-only). Each proposal card renders exactly as an existing rule row renders: RULE_TYPE_LABELS heading + summarize() text + the enforcement line — both helpers are already exported from AvailabilitySettings.tsx (:45, :193). Actions per card: Create fires the EXISTING useCreateAvailabilityRule (:27-32; its invalidateKeys already refresh the list) with {rule_type, enforcement, params} verbatim; Edit renders the exported RuleForm (:451) with initialRule built from the proposal (id/user_id empty, timestamps null) and onSubmit wired to the same create hook, so parsed values populate the form for edit-before-save. The type picker being disabled under initialRule (:502) is accepted: changing type means retyping the sentence or using the manual form. could_not_parse renders the reason with no Create affordance. The model's human_summary renders as secondary explainer text only — the structured preview is always derived client-side from the params via summarize(), so what the user confirms is what will be created. No new write path exists anywhere.

8. LOGGING SHAPE, decided: the free text and the model's raw output are NEVER logged at any level — the input is therapist-authored schedule prose, but free text can incidentally carry a person's name. Log only input length, proposal count, and rule_type values; failure paths log exception class/context like note_import_service.py:483-485 without embedding the input. The gateway's telemetry span records operation/model/token counts only (structured_llm_gateway.py:186, :200-207).

SEQUENCING / FENCING: lands AFTER PABLO-bhz and PABLO-mep, both already specced against the same surfaces. AvailabilitySettings.tsx is the shared hub file — bhz owns the empty-state seed affordance, mep owns the session-defaults fields section; this bead's diff there is one import + one mount line, rebased onto whatever landed. backend/app/routes/scheduling.py is also shared — mep edits the /api/availability/slots route (:699-714); this bead only APPENDS a parse route + models, so the rebase is mechanical. If mep has landed, the enum carries a ninth settings-owned value — excluded from parse by the explicit allow-list, and mep's picker test is untouched by this bead. Do NOT touch: backend/app/scheduling_engine/ (slot computation, conflict checking, repositories), the existing create/update/delete routes.

OUT OF SCOPE: block_date_range / block_specific_dates parsing (v1 exclusion above); any relative-date or timezone handling; new rule types; parsing for settings-owned rule types; changes to the structured form's behavior; persistence of parse text or history; streaming; voice input; retry logic beyond the gateway's built-ins.

FILES: backend/app/routes/scheduling.py, backend/app/models/scheduling.py, backend/app/services/availability_parse_service.py (new), backend/app/rate_limit.py, backend/app/settings.py, backend/tests/test_availability_parse_service.py (new), backend/tests/test_scheduling_routes.py, frontend/src/components/settings/NaturalLanguageRuleEntry.tsx (new), frontend/src/components/settings/AvailabilitySettings.tsx (mount only), frontend/src/lib/api/availability.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useAvailability.ts, frontend/src/components/settings/__tests__/NaturalLanguageRuleEntry.test.tsx (new), frontend/src/components/settings/__tests__/AvailabilitySettings.test.tsx (one mount assertion).

DONE SIGNAL: exactly one PR; make check green (ruff + ruff format + mypy + pytest); frontend vitest + tsc green; zero diff under backend/app/scheduling_engine/.

EXCLUSIVITY SEMANTICS (pinned 2026-08-18, post-spec addendum): phrasing like "I ONLY meet on Mondays 1-3 and Tuesdays 2-4" is creates-only in v1. The engine is whitelist-based (a day with no working_hours rule yields zero slots), so on a rule-free setup the created rules fully implement the exclusivity with nothing else needed. When OTHER working_hours rules already exist for days not mentioned, the parse response includes a non-blocking notice enumerating them (rule ids + human summaries) so the confirm UI can display "you also have working hours on Wednesday - remove them in the rules list if you no longer meet then." The parser NEVER proposes deletions or modifications of existing rules in v1 - creates only. The schema gains an optional exclusive: bool on the response plus an existing_conflicting_rules list the route populates from the user's current rules (cheap read on the already-loaded rules).
acceptance_criteria:
All CI-verifiable; no live LLM anywhere. The fake is FakeStructuredLLMGateway (backend/app/services/structured_llm_gateway.py:562-607 — queued responses / default_response, recorded calls for prompt assertions), injected into the service exactly as backend/tests/test_note_import_service.py:96-97 does.

1. Service tests — backend/tests/test_availability_parse_service.py (new):
   (a) "No appointments on Fridays" with a queued StructuredCompletion proposing block_day_of_week {"day_of_week": 4} round-trips into exactly one validated proposal with those params and enforcement "hard".
   (b) "9 to 5 on weekdays" with a queued five-proposal working_hours response (day_of_week 0..4, "09:00"-"17:00") returns five individually listed proposals.
   (c) Schema-violating gateway output is rejected, not passed through: rule_type outside the covered six (block_date_range, an unknown string, and — post-sibling-landing — any settings-owned type), day_of_week 7, end <= start, negative buffer minutes, max_per_day 0: each yields could_not_parse with a reason and zero proposals carrying the bad payload.

   (g) The covered-type frozenset equals the six date-free types and every member is asserted to be a valid RuleType (backend/app/scheduling_engine/models/availability.py:13-21) — enum growth fails this test until coverage is widened deliberately.

POST /api/availability/rules/parse returns 200 with proposals; the InMemoryAvailabilityRuleRepository is asserted EMPTY after the parse (the endpoint creates no rows); the existing create-route coverage (:386-405) passes unchanged, pinning that rule creation still happens only via POST /api/availability/rules; a limiter stub whose check() raises yields 429, proving the route is rate-limit-gated; auth resolves through the standard get_tenant_context override (backend/tests/conftest.py:351) like every sibling availability route — no new auth surface.

   (a) Submitting text renders the structured preview using the same rendering as an existing rule row — the card text equals summarize() output for the proposal (e.g. "Friday blocked" for block_day_of_week {"day_of_week": 4}) under its RULE_TYPE_LABELS heading.
   (b) Clicking Create fires the existing create-hook mock exactly once with {rule_type, enforcement, params} verbatim; rendering + a successful parse alone fires zero create calls (nothing is created without the explicit click).

   (e) Edit opens the RuleForm populated with the parsed values; submitting it fires the create hook with the edited params.

Existing RuleForm and rules-list behavior is untouched.

title: Session length, breaks, and start-time alignment as first-class availability settings

title: Sign-out is unreachable when the auth session is stale
description: When the browser's auth session goes stale (expired token that failed to refresh — e.g. a tab left open overnight or a laptop waking from sleep), the app keeps rendering the signed-in shell while every API call returns 401. The UI is inert, and the sign-out control itself depends on an API round-trip, so clicking it does nothing. The user cannot self-rescue: the only ways out are manually clearing cookies or knowing to type the logout URL by hand. Observed 2026-08-18 during local testing; this failure shape is invisible in logs-first triage because nothing errors client-side.
design:
SPEC (spec pass 2026-08-18, drafting agent). Direction decided at triage; this pass verifies mechanism against the code and pins pointers. Two changes, both frontend.

PROBLEM, verified:
A stale session means the auth cookie still verifies (12h maxAge — src/lib/auth-config.ts:9,:53) while the backend rejects the bearer token, so the middleware keeps serving the signed-in shell while every API call 401s. Two client-side gaps keep the user stuck:

(a) DETECTION GAP. The centralized 401 seam already exists: apiClient boots unrecoverable 401s to /login via handleTerminalAuthLogout (src/lib/api/client.ts:315-321; getBlob mirror :425-431; the handler itself :68-85 — provider signOut({wipePersisted:true}) then window.location.assign('/login?reason=…'), re-entry-guarded at :52). But the boot fires ONLY for envelope codes in TERMINAL_AUTH_CODES (:158-163) or IDLE_TIMEOUT. A 401 whose body carries no error envelope — the backend renders a plain-detail HTTPException as FastAPI-default {"detail": …} and logs it as "auth failed: UNKNOWN" (backend/app/api_errors.py:112-124 maps missing envelope code to UNKNOWN, log line :144; e.g. the bare fallback raise in backend/app/auth/providers.py:318) — maps to errorCode "UNKNOWN_ERROR" client-side (client.ts:300) and boots NOTHING. That is exactly the observed failure signature: repeated 401 "auth failed: UNKNOWN" on /api/auth/session while the shell renders inert. (The server-side rescue only covers full RSC loads: app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:92-98 redirects any 401 to /login?reason=…; a tab already rendered never re-runs it.)

(b) SIGN-OUT CONTROL. Header (src/components/layout/Header.tsx:24-31, wired at :85) awaits getClientAuthProvider().signOut() — for the default firebase provider that is firebaseSignOut (src/lib/auth/firebase/client.ts:284-300): SDK sign-out plus an UNBOUNDED fetch("/api/logout") at :296 (contrast syncAuthTick's /api/login fetch, which IS withTimeout-bounded at :167-175) — then a soft router.push("/login") with no reason param. Failure modes: any hang before the push leaves the click doing nothing; and if the cookie-clear fetch didn't land, the /login push bounces straight back to /dashboard (authenticated-on-/login redirect, src/lib/auth/firebase/middleware.ts:65-67).

KEY FACT — /api/logout is ALREADY reachable with no or invalid session; no public-paths change is needed. proxy.ts:15 routes it into the middleware, and next-firebase-auth-edge short-circuits loginPath/logoutPath BEFORE any token verification (node_modules/next-firebase-auth-edge/lib/next/middleware.js:110-121 -> createAuthMiddlewareResponse :71-87), answering the logout path with removeAuthCookies — a 200 {"success":true} JSON carrying the cookie-removal Set-Cookie headers (lib/next/cookies/index.js:122-132). PUBLIC_PATHS (src/lib/auth/firebase/middleware.ts:17) stays untouched. Consequence: a top-level navigation to /api/logout clears cookies but strands the user on a JSON body — so the middleware must answer NAVIGATIONS to logoutPath with a redirect to /login carrying those same cookie-removal headers.

MECHANISM:
1. Sign-out as navigation to logoutPath.
   a. Middleware (src/lib/auth/firebase/middleware.ts): when the request path is logoutPath AND the request is a top-level navigation (Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate, with Accept: text/html as fallback), take the library's logout response and return a redirect to /login instead, COPYING its Set-Cookie removal headers verbatim — never re-deriving them (flags and enableMultipleCookies behavior, auth-config.ts:48-56, must be byte-identical; cookie flags are a closed decision). fetch() callers (firebase/client.ts:122,:143,:296 — cors mode) keep today's 200 JSON. Forward a whitelisted reason query param (only values in FORCED_LOGOUT_REASONS, src/lib/auth/forced-logout.ts:16) from the logout URL onto the /login redirect. Also handle the DEV_MODE branch (middleware.ts:49-51 currently skips everything): redirect logoutPath navigations to /login there too — no app route exists for /api/logout (frontend/app/api has only auth/ and config/), so today a dev-mode navigation would 404.
   b. Header.tsx handleSignOut: bound the provider sign-out (best-effort; withTimeout already exists, firebase/client.ts:100-106) and pass {wipePersisted:true} (same bfcache rationale as client.ts:72-79), then HARD-navigate window.location.assign(logoutPath) (imported from @/lib/auth-config) instead of router.push. One navigation clears cookies and lands on /login in the same response — nothing to bounce, nothing for a dead session to block. PROVIDER CAUTION: oidcSignOut self-navigates to the IdP end-session URL (src/lib/auth/oidc/client.ts:163) and must keep owning its navigation — gate the Header's logoutPath assign so it never stomps that redirect (e.g. only for the firebase provider, or let the provider contract own the terminal navigation).
2. Unclassifiable 401 = terminal. In apiClient's 401 branch (client.ts:315-321) and getBlob's (:425-431): for client-managed-token requests (!token), a 401 whose body yields no recognized envelope code (errorCode UNKNOWN_ERROR — i.e. not MFA_REQUIRED, not IDLE_TIMEOUT, not in TERMINAL_AUTH_CODES) is treated as terminal -> handleTerminalAuthLogout("session_expired"). The refresh-retry gate (:248-253) is NOT widened — closed decision. MFA_REQUIRED stays excluded; IDLE_TIMEOUT keeps its own reason; the re-entry guard is unchanged. This makes the inert shell self-resolving: the first 401 from any call — including the IdleTimeout session peek (src/lib/api/session.ts:24-26, fired from src/components/IdleTimeout.tsx:102) — lands on /login?reason=session_expired, which the middleware lets render (isForcedLogoutArrival, forced-logout.ts:18-20, consumed at firebase/middleware.ts:65) and where LoginScreen clears the stale client session itself (src/lib/auth/firebase/LoginScreen.tsx:52-75 -> clearStaleSession, firebase/client.ts:114-126). If routing the terminal flow itself through logoutPath (assign logoutPath?reason=… so the cookie clear and the landing are one response) proves clean with 1a's reason forwarding, prefer it; otherwise handleTerminalAuthLogout's existing /login?reason=… landing stands.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: sign-out must work without a working API session; the redirect target is the existing logoutPath, not a new route; middleware auth semantics, cookie flags, and Secure-cookie behavior unchanged (the navigation answer copies the library's cookie-removal headers verbatim and changes no verification outcome on any path); do not touch token refresh logic (the :248-253 retry gate stays as-is), the login flow (LoginScreen untouched), or the public-paths list (verified unnecessary — logoutPath is handled pre-verification, pointers above).

OUT OF SCOPE: backend error envelopes (giving providers.py:318 a proper code is a separate bead — the client must tolerate unclassifiable 401s regardless, since any proxy or edge layer can also produce one); LoginScreen / forced-logout reason set; OIDC logout redesign (its self-navigation just must not regress); idle-timeout semantics; any new route.

SEQUENCING: siblings PABLO-bhz and PABLO-mep live in settings/calendar/availability surfaces (dashboard settings page, src/components/settings/, src/components/calendar/, scheduling engine) — checked against this bead's file set below: ZERO overlap, safe to run in parallel with both.

DONE SIGNAL: the unclassifiable-401 test is red on current main and green with the change (state red-then-green in the PR body); frontend vitest + lint green; exactly one PR.

title: Appointment dialog can only book the first 20 patients
description:
## Problem

`AppointmentModal.tsx` calls `usePatientList()` with no params. The backend default is `page_size=20` (`backend/app/routes/patients.py`), so the New appointment dialog's patient `Select` renders only the first 20 patients — `patients.map()` over one unpaginated page, with no search input.

Patients sort by `last_name, first_name`, so which 20 you get is alphabetical. A clinician with more than 20 patients simply cannot book an appointment for anyone outside that window: the option is not in the DOM, and there is no way to search for it from the dialog.

## Why it matters

21+ patients is an ordinary caseload for an established practice. For those users the calendar's primary create path is broken for most of their roster, with no workaround and no error message — the patient just isn't in the list.

## Related

PABLO-y93 fixed exactly this class of bug for the patient LIST (page_size=100 + 'showing N of M'), but the appointment dialog was not part of that change and still has the original default.
design:
## DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate

**Build the searchable typeahead. Do not simply raise page_size.** `GET /api/patients` already accepts a `search` param; query it server-side as the user types so roster size stops mattering. Raising `page_size` to 100 only moves the ceiling (the endpoint caps at 100) and would not satisfy the acceptance criteria, which require a practice above 100 patients to work.

**Debounce input ~250ms** and keep the currently-selected patient rendered even when it falls outside the active result set, so an edit-existing-appointment open does not blank the field.

**Keep the empty query working:** with no text typed, show the first page as today, so the common small-practice case is unchanged and needs no typing.

## Where

- `frontend/src/components/calendar/AppointmentModal.tsx` — the patient control is a plain shadcn `Select` today (`patients.map()` over `usePatientList()`); swap it for a `Command`/combobox that accepts input.
- `frontend/src/hooks/usePatients.ts` — `usePatientList` already takes params; pass `search` through. Do not change its signature for other callers.

## Do NOT touch

- `PatientTable.tsx` and the patient-list pagination — that surface was already fixed under PABLO-y93 and is out of scope here. Changing it widens the diff into a file this bead does not own.
- The backend route, its response model, or the appointment POST payload. This is a frontend-only change; the API already has everything needed.

## Tests

`frontend/src/components/calendar/__tests__/AppointmentModal.test.tsx` — add a case for selecting a patient that is NOT in the first page of results (i.e. only reachable via search).
acceptance_criteria:
- A practice with more than 100 patients can find and book any patient from the New appointment dialog.
- Selecting a patient still books correctly (POST /api/appointments unchanged).
- The dialog's existing unit tests pass, with a new case covering a patient outside the first page.
- No change to the appointment payload or backend route signature.
notes:
EVIDENCE STRENGTHENED 2026-08-15: this is not only a UX ceiling, it is actively breaking the deployed e2e gate, and the breakage is progressive rather than a clean pass/fail.

Measured against the shared test tenant: soft-deleting every patient made the scheduling e2e pass immediately; an hour of runs re-accumulated patients (~2 per run) and the same spec degraded in lockstep with the count — passed at 0 active patients, intermittent around 20-30 (a new patient sometimes still fell inside the first page, because patients sort by last_name,first_name so inclusion is alphabetical luck), and failed on every run at 44.

The user-visible consequence at >20 patients is worse than 'cannot find the patient': the picker silently offers no matching option, and an appointment can end up booked against the wrong patient or none at all rather than failing loudly. That is the part worth fixing carefully.

Practical note for whoever takes this: raising page_size is not enough even as a stopgap, because the ceiling just moves to 100 and the same silent-wrong-selection behaviour returns. The search-backed typeahead in the design section removes the ceiling entirely.

PR merged (https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/704) — reconciled
